arms.description: production JS fallback solver (src/solver/naive-solver.js) — baseline arm and fallback engine
2048-solver submodule strategies compiled natively (g++), driven through the persistent shim; separately labelled build, not the WASM arm
same C++ sources built by Emscripten through the extension's embind surface; included only when the local build succeeds

rules.spawnPolicy: frozen per-seed streams of (uCell, uValue) draws from spawn-history.json; standard empty-cell selection with 10% four-tile odds; every arm replays the identical stream for a seed
rules.moveModel: game state advances only through test/helpers/reference-2048.mjs; solver-internal simulators are never trusted to advance state
rules.fallback: on time-budget overrun, engine error, or no legal entry in the engine's order, the naive arm supplies the move (canonical Up,Right,Down,Left order if naive is unavailable); raw engine output is still committed
rules.purity: naive and scripted arms are considered purer than native-cpp and wasm because every part of their move production is JS; native-cpp/wasm carry the cross-language convention risk that the native-crosscheck test pins down
rules.strategyEncoding: type and heuristic are the SUBMODULE STRINGS (expectimax-depth, corner) — the shim and embind factory both match on names; numeric codes would silently fall back to defaults. depth=3 is the deepest expectimax depth whose measured latency (~10 ms median, this machine) fits the 200 ms per-move budget; depth 4 measured ~300 ms and overruns.

scopeNote: Results are machine-specific measurements on 20 seeds. They carry no universal latency or performance claim.
